entries.name: non-pair-tuple-operand-eq-any-concrete-v3-box#0
entries.description: `sigmaProp(ByIndex((1,2,3),0) == 1)` — an `SAny` operand against an `SInt` one. `check2(SameType)` in the deserialization builder refuses it, `ConstraintFailed`, so the tree never parses. THE ROW THE SIGMA-RUST SESSION CORRECTED ITSELF ON: it first read this as an eval-time `checkType` failure, then re-read the builder and expected a parse refusal. It is a parse refusal. **SEPARATING:** an implementation that parses this and fails later accepts a box the JVM cannot even read.

entries.name: non-pair-tuple-operand-gt-any-concrete-v3-box#1
entries.description: `sigmaProp(ByIndex((1,2,3),0) > 1)` — the same operands under a COMPARISON. Refused too, but by a different constraint: `comparisonOp` runs `check2(OnlyNumeric)` at `:699` first, and `SAny` is not numeric. Same outcome, different reason, which matters to anyone implementing one check and reusing it. **SEPARATING.**

entries.name: non-pair-tuple-operand-gt-any-any-v3-box#2
entries.description: `sigmaProp(t(0) > t(1))` — BOTH operands `SAny`. Still REJECTED: the numeric constraint is about each operand's type and not about the two agreeing, so **a comparison has no escape** where equality does. The row that proves the next one is not a general leniency. **SEPARATING.**

entries.name: non-pair-tuple-operand-eq-any-any-v3-box#3
entries.description: `sigmaProp(t(0) == t(1))` — BOTH operands `SAny`, under EQUALITY, and it **ACCEPTS**: `check2(SameType)` is satisfied, so the tree parses and round-trips to its own bytes. THE KEYSTONE OF THE FAMILY, and a cross-tier pair: the eval tier's `Tuple.non_pair_value_gates` G1/G2 is this very tree failing at EVAL with `Unknown type SAny`. So this is a box anyone can create, whose script no one can satisfy. **SEPARATING BOTH WAYS:** an implementation that refuses it at parse over-rejects a valid box, and one that evaluates the comparison over-accepts a spend.

entries.name: non-pair-tuple-operand-eq-concrete-control-v3-box#4
entries.description: **THE CONTROL** — `sigmaProp(ByIndex(Coll[Int](1,2,3),0) == 1)`, the same shape over an ordinary collection: ACCEPTED, round-trip identity, and it evaluates to a `SigmaProp` too. It is what shows the four rejects above are the `SAny` operand's doing and not `ByIndex` under an equality.
